tagline: The yachting capital of the eastern Caribbean and the natural hub of the Leewards fan.
summary: Antigua's English and Falmouth Harbours form the eastern Caribbean's premier yachting centre (home of Antigua Sailing Week and the Superyacht Challenge), and its sister island Barbuda offers pristine, low-density luxury (Barbuda Belle, the Robert De Niro-backed Nobu Beach Inn). Antigua sits centrally among the Leewards, a Pioneer II hop to its own coast and cays and a Quanta-LR/Pioneer-edge link to St Kitts, Guadeloupe and St-Barths.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: Pioneer II owns Antigua's coast and cays, the Antigua↔Barbuda crossing (~30 nm), and the Pioneer-edge hops to St Kitts and Guadeloupe (~45 nm).
navier_fit.quanta_lr: Quanta-LR (H2 2026+) connects Antigua to the St-Barths/St-Maarten cluster (~60 nm) and down the Lesser Antilles spine.

competitive_landscape: The Barbuda Express ferry, superyacht tenders, and a busy charter fleet operate today — demand proof and partners. The Barbuda ferry's weather cancellations are the clearest pain. There is no foiling incumbent.
seasonality: Atlantic hurricane season (Jun–Nov) is the constraint (Barbuda was devastated by Irma in 2017); yachting high season is Dec–Apr with the regattas in spring.
regulatory_note: Independent state; Antigua & Barbuda Dept of Marine Services & Merchant Shipping (ADOMS) is a large ship registry and a capable certification counterpart. Port Authority + Tourism Authority procurement.
key_partners: Jumby Bay / Nobu Barbuda / Barbuda Belle

precedents.why_it_matters: Antigua plays the same yachting-hub role for the Leewards that the Virgins play to their north.
